places.name: Boston Common
places.summary: America's oldest public park is a practical downtown base for Frog Pond seasonal skating and spray play, Tadpole Playground, ballfields, monuments, the Freedom Trail, lawns, and major civic events.
places.hours: Boston parks generally close from 11:30 p.m. to 6 a.m. Frog Pond, the Visitor Information Center, restrooms, programs, and events have separate seasonal schedules.
places.cost: General park access, Tadpole Playground, monuments, and summer Frog Pond spray play are free. Winter skating, rentals, food, parking, and some programs cost separately.
places.parking: There is no surface visitor lot. The paid Boston Common Garage beneath the park is convenient, but transit is usually simpler and events can restrict streets and garage access.
places.arrival: Use Park Street for the Freedom Trail, Brewer Fountain, and Visitor Center; Beacon Street for Frog Pond and the State House; Charles Street for the playground and Public Garden crossing.
places.restrooms: Public restrooms are near the Visitor Information Center and Frog Pond when those facilities are open. Do not assume late-night or event access.
places.accessibility: Primary paved walks and major entrances provide stair-free routes, but the Common is rolling terrain with historic paving, winter ice, lawn grades, and event barriers.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed outside posted dog-free areas; designated off-leash use has separate rules. Dogs are not allowed in Tadpole Playground or Frog Pond facilities.
places.family: Frog Pond, Tadpole Playground, lawns, monuments, and short Freedom Trail connections make a strong family stop. Check seasonal water or skating status before promising the activity.
places.transit: Park Street station is beside the Common; Boylston, Downtown Crossing, and multiple bus routes are also close. Transit avoids scarce and expensive downtown parking.
places.need: Choose the exact side before arriving. Large demonstrations, festivals, winter ice, summer heat, thunderstorms, and Frog Pond closures can change the best route.
subsites: Flagstaff Hill and Soldiers and Sailors Monument
Robert Gould Shaw and 54th Regiment Memorial

places.name: Public Garden
places.summary: America's first public botanical garden centers on a lagoon, seasonal Swan Boats, the Make Way for Ducklings statues, ornamental plantings, historic monuments, and a compact walking loop beside Boston Common.
places.hours: The garden follows Boston park closure hours, generally closing 11:30 p.m.-6 a.m. Swan Boats run seasonally and weather permitting on their own daily schedule.
places.cost: Garden access and monuments are free. Swan Boats charge per ride; parking, food, and special programs cost separately.
places.parking: There is no public lot in the garden. Use transit, nearby paid garages, or legal metered parking; Boston Common Garage is across Charles Street.
places.arrival: Enter from Charles Street for the shortest connection from Boston Common, or use Arlington Street for the George Washington statue and Back Bay. The lagoon loop reaches all major landmarks.
places.restrooms: There is no dependable general-purpose restroom inside the Public Garden. Use confirmed-open facilities on Boston Common or nearby businesses before settling in.
places.accessibility: Main garden paths and lagoon approaches are generally accessible, but historic surfaces, bridge grades, crowds, snow, ice, and temporary work can affect routes.
places.dogs: Pets are not allowed in the Public Garden except qualifying service animals. Do not use Boston Common dog rules for this separate park.
places.family: Duckling statues and Swan Boats are the family anchors. The lawns and flower beds are protected landscapes, so use paths and benches rather than treating the garden as a play field.
places.transit: Arlington and Boylston stations serve opposite ends; Park Street is across Boston Common. Pick the station nearest the landmark you want.
places.need: Swan Boats are seasonal, weather dependent, and can pause for high winds or storms. Flower displays, bridge access, and event routes also change through the year.
subsites: George Washington Statue and Arlington entrance
Wendell Phillips Statue and Boylston entrance

places.name: Charles River Esplanade
places.operator: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
places.summary: Boston's central riverfront park combines paved walking and cycling paths, playgrounds, lagoons, docks, boating, lawns, public art, the Hatch Shell, and skyline views within the larger Charles River Reservation.
places.hours: The Charles River Reservation is officially open sunrise to sunset. Playgrounds, boating, restrooms, concessions, events, and the Hatch Shell use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, path, playground, lawn, and public-art access is free. Boating, rentals, parking, food, and ticketed events may charge.
places.parking: The Esplanade has very limited direct parking. Transit, walking, and cycling are usually best; nearby garages and meters are paid and event traffic can close approaches.
places.arrival: Pedestrian bridges cross Storrow Drive at several points. Choose the bridge nearest Hatch Shell, Playspace, Community Boating, or the lagoons instead of navigating to the broad park center.
places.restrooms: Seasonal public facilities serve the busiest Esplanade areas, but coverage is not continuous along the river. Locate an open restroom before a long walk.
places.accessibility: Major river paths are paved, but bridge approaches, slopes, construction detours, crowds, snow, ice, and waterfront edges vary by segment.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under DCR rules. Keep pets out of playgrounds, athletic use, planted areas, and water where posted, and clean up waste.
places.family: The Playspace, Stoneman Playground, lagoons, docks, lawns, and boats offer strong family options. Fast bicycles and exposed water edges require close supervision.
places.transit: Charles/MGH is useful for the east end; Arlington, Park Street, and Back Bay routes require a longer walk. Use the exact footbridge as the trip destination.
places.need: Check Hatch Shell events, path construction, boating status, river advisories, heat, thunderstorms, wind, snow, and ice. Storrow Drive makes missed entrances costly.

places.name: Franklin Park
places.summary: Boston's 485-acre Olmsted country park includes wooded trails, Scarboro Pond, Playstead fields, multiple playgrounds, historic Bear Dens and ruins, golf, White Stadium, and the separately operated Franklin Park Zoo.
places.hours: Boston parks generally close 11:30 p.m.-6 a.m. The zoo, golf course, White Stadium, playground spray features, restrooms, events, and construction zones have separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, trail, lawn, playground, and landmark access is free. The zoo, golf, reservations, parking for some attractions, food, and programs cost separately.
places.parking: Parking is distributed around the 485-acre park. Navigate to the zoo, Playstead, Tiffany Moore Tot Lot, golf clubhouse, Scarboro Pond, or another exact destination before driving.
places.arrival: Franklin Park is too large for one universal entrance. Blue Hill Avenue serves the zoo and golf side; Seaver Street serves Playstead and Tiffany Moore; Walnut Avenue reaches western landscapes.
places.restrooms: Facilities are concentrated near staffed attractions, fields, playgrounds, and the golf or zoo areas. Remote woodland routes do not have dependable restroom coverage.
places.accessibility: Improved entrances and paved routes connect many developed destinations, but wooded trails, steep grades, roots, pond edges, construction, and long distances vary substantially.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in general park areas. Franklin Park does not currently provide a confirmed permanent off-leash dog park; keep dogs out of playgrounds and restricted attractions.
places.family: Use Tiffany Moore Tot Lot for documented accessible play and spray play, or choose the zoo separately. The Wilderness and pond are better for older children prepared for a longer walk.
places.transit: Several MBTA routes serve different edges. Route 16 connects the zoo and golf side with Forest Hills and Andrew; choose transit based on the exact destination.
places.need: White Stadium and pathway projects can alter roads, parking, and paths. Check construction, field events, zoo traffic, heat, thunderstorms, snow, ice, and woodland conditions.
subsites: Tiffany Moore Tot Lot and spray play
Elma Lewis Playstead and White Stadium
Historic Bear Dens and Overlook Ruins

places.name: Arnold Arboretum
places.summary: This free 281-acre living museum holds more than 15,000 accessioned plants, broad paved roads, woodland paths, skyline views, seasonal collections, family activities, and a staffed visitor center.
places.hours: The landscape is open daily sunrise to sunset. The Hunnewell Visitor Center is generally open daily 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; programs and facilities can differ.
places.cost: Landscape admission, the Visitor Center, self-guided exploration, and general programs are free unless a specific event says otherwise.
places.parking: Free street parking is available along Arborway, Flora Way, and Walter Street. Accessible spaces are at Arborway, Forest Hills, Walter Street, and Centre Street gates.
places.arrival: Use 125 Arborway for the Visitor Center and orientation, Peters Hill Gate for the skyline hill, or Forest Hills Gate for transit. The grounds are large and hilly.
places.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are in the Hunnewell Building from 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; accessible portable restrooms are near Arborway Gate, Hemlock Hill Road, and Peters Hill.
places.accessibility: Paved roads provide many routes, but natural terrain and trails vary. Reserved weekday driving permits and free manual wheelchairs support visitors with access needs.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in the landscape under visitor guidelines; service animals are welcome in the landscape and Visitor Center. Protect collections and clean up waste.
places.family: Free family activities, labeled trees, wildlife, hills, and open exploration work well for children. Bring water and choose a shorter loop for strollers or young walkers.
places.transit: Forest Hills station and nearby bus routes serve the south side; walking and cycling connections reach other gates. The Visitor Center is not at every entrance.
places.need: Blooms and foliage are seasonal, hills are steeper than the map suggests, and paths can be icy or muddy. Check storms, heat, wind, ticks, restroom hours, and gate location.

places.name: Castle Island
places.operator: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
places.summary: Castle Island combines the Fort Independence loop, harbor and airport views, Pleasure Bay swimming, playground and picnic areas, fishing, restrooms, rinsing showers, and the seasonal Sullivan's food stand.
places.hours: The reservation is open sunrise to sunset. Fort tours, lifeguards, restrooms, showers, concessions, and events use seasonal or separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, beach, loop, playground, and fort exterior access is free. Food, bus parking, and some organized activities cost separately.
places.parking: A free lot is near Fort Independence, with metered street parking along the beaches. Summer weekends and special events fill early and may use traffic controls.
places.arrival: Use 2010 Day Boulevard for the fort, loop, playground, restrooms, and Sullivan's. Continue west around Pleasure Bay only if your goal is the longer beach loop.
places.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are available at Castle Island and Carson Beach; rinsing showers and first-aid or lifeguard facilities are seasonal.
places.accessibility: The site has accessible restrooms, an accessible Pleasure Bay trail, seasonal beach mats and beach wheelchairs, and accessible picnicking at Carson Beach.
places.dogs: Dogs are allowed under DCR rules but are prohibited on beaches May 1 through September 15. Leash and cleanup requirements still apply elsewhere.
places.family: The short fort loop, playground, planes and ships, beach, picnic space, and food make an easy family outing. Supervise closely at seawalls and water.
places.transit: The area is transit friendly, but the final walk can be exposed. Cycling and rideshare are useful when the lot is full; confirm return service after events.
places.need: Check water quality, lifeguard status, tide, wind, heat, thunderstorms, fort-tour hours, event security, and parking. Swimming is only safe when conditions permit.

places.name: Rose Fitzgerald Kennedy Greenway
places.summary: The 1.5-mile downtown ribbon links Chinatown, the Financial District, waterfront, and North End through gardens, seven water attractions, rotating public art, a universal-design carousel, food vendors, and hundreds of free events.
places.hours: The Greenway is open 7 a.m.-11 p.m. Carousel, fountains, food vendors, drinkeries, markets, and events use separate seasonal schedules.
places.cost: Park, gardens, fountains, public art, and most Conservancy events are free. Carousel rides are currently $4; food, drinks, parking, and special programs cost separately.
places.parking: There is no public parking on the Greenway. Use nearby garages, Atlantic Avenue meters, transit, ferries, walking, or cycling; rates and event restrictions vary.
places.arrival: Choose Chinatown/Dewey Square, Wharf District and Rings Fountain, Carousel/Harbor side, or North End parks before traveling. The full park is 1.5 miles long.
places.restrooms: The linear park does not provide continuous dedicated restroom coverage. Use confirmed-open public facilities at adjacent transportation, market, harbor, or cultural destinations.
places.accessibility: All Greenway paths are maintained as ADA-compliant, and the Carousel uses universal design for physical, sensory, and cognitive access.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed; clean up waste and keep pets out of garden beds. Smoking, alcohol outside permitted operations, and wheeled recreation on park paths are restricted.
places.family: Seven water attractions, the native-animal Carousel, lawns, art, food, and frequent free programs are family highlights. Fountain and event operations change daily.
places.transit: South Station, Downtown Crossing, Haymarket, Government Center, Aquarium, State Street, North Station, buses, and ferries serve different sections.
places.need: Check the live calendar and exact parcel. Fountains, Carousel, vendors, markets, public art, and drinkeries are seasonal; events can occupy lawns and plazas.

places.name: Jamaica Pond
places.summary: This deep spring-fed Emerald Necklace pond supports a scenic loop, seasonal rowboat and sailboat rentals, fishing, running, biking, ranger programs, concerts, and quiet shoreline views.
places.hours: Boston parks generally close 11:30 p.m.-6 a.m. Boat rentals, boathouse, nature programs, restrooms, concerts, and seasonal operations have separate schedules.
places.cost: General pond, path, fishing access with required license, and public programs are free unless posted. Boat rentals and some programs cost separately.
places.parking: Parking immediately around the pond is limited and mostly legal street parking. Transit, walking, or cycling can be easier during warm weekends and events.
places.arrival: Use 507 Jamaicaway for the boathouse and orientation. Pick the boathouse, Pinebank side, fishing access, or a loop entrance before arriving because road crossings divide approaches.
places.restrooms: Restroom access is concentrated near the boathouse and staffed program areas and can be seasonal. Do not assume a facility is open along every part of the loop.
places.accessibility: Much of the pond loop is developed, but grades, roots, road crossings, shore edges, winter conditions, and unpaved segments vary. Start near the boathouse for services.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under Boston park rules. Keep pets controlled around runners, wildlife, fishing lines, boats, and narrow shoreline paths.
places.family: The loop, boats, fishing views, wildlife, and ranger programs work for families, but the pond is more than 50 feet deep and has no casual swimming access.
places.transit: Bus routes and Emerald Necklace paths serve Jamaica Plain. Use the boathouse as the destination when you need rentals or visitor services.
places.need: Private boats are not allowed. Check rental status, fishing license rules, storms, heat, wind, water conditions, path ice, and limited parking before visiting.
subsites: Ward's Pond and Emerald Necklace connection
